headline: Tanker Traffic Through Strait of Hormuz Rises Despite Attacks
summary: The number of energy-carrying tankers transiting the Strait of Hormuz increased in November, averaging over 26 per day, despite attacks and mine incidents hitting the highest level since the beginning of the Iran war.
why: The Strait of Hormuz is a critical global chokepoint for international crude oil and liquefied natural gas shipments, meaning security incidents directly threaten global energy supplies.

impacts.name: Brent crude
impacts.why: Increased tanker traffic through the key oil transit chokepoint affects global energy supply flows.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: The 7-day moving average showed more than 26 crude oil, fuel, and LNG tankers transiting the Strait daily despite rising security incidents.
